summary: Kazakhstan waives visas for around 80 nationalities — including the EU, US, UK and China — for 30 days per visit, lets CIS and EAEU citizens enter freely for up to 90 days, and offers an eVisa via the official Visa-Migration Portal for most other travelers.

Fees vary by nationality and reciprocity. Confirm with the Kazakh consulate serving your place of residence.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from Kazakhstan; some airlines apply a 6-month rule, so carrying 6 months' validity is the safe choice.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. WHO records no minimum age for Kazakhstan, and any transit through such a country's airport counts, however short the stop.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked for visa-free entry, but visa applicants may be asked to show medical coverage and healthcare is fee-based for visitors — comprehensive travel insurance is strongly recommended.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

onwardTicket.text: No formal requirement, though border officers occasionally ask about onward plans and accommodation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show means of support for the stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

declarations.name: Arrival notification (migration registration by host)
declarations.text: Your host — hotel, landlord or inviting organization — must notify the migration authorities of your arrival within 3 working days. Hotels do this automatically; if you stay privately, make sure your host files the notification, as fines can fall on both sides.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

currencyLimits.text: Cash of US$10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on entry and exit under Eurasian Economic Union rules.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan

notes: Standard EAEU duty-free allowances apply for alcohol and tobacco. Confirm current limits before travel.
Medicines containing controlled substances need a prescription and may have to be declared.

payments.text: Cards and Kaspi QR payments dominate in Almaty and Astana, but carry tenge for bazaars, intercity taxis and anywhere rural.

safety.text: Kazakhstan is generally safe for travelers. Petty crime occurs in cities. Use ride-hailing apps rather than unmarked taxis, and take normal care at night and around bazaars.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Kazakhstan Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May–September is best for the steppe, the mountains around Almaty and the lakes; winters are severely cold, though good for skiing at Shymbulak.

idp.text: Kazakhstan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Kazakhstan is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Kazakhstan yet.

tips.text: Hotels register your arrival with the migration service automatically — if you stay in a private apartment, make sure your host files the arrival notification within 3 working days.
Kazakhstan moved the whole country to a single UTC+5 time zone in 2024 — older timetables, maps and devices may still show two zones.
The climate is fiercely continental: winters routinely drop below −20°C and summers on the steppe top 35°C. Plan clothing and travel timing accordingly.
Yandex Go and inDrive are the standard way to get around cities; agree nothing with kerbside cabs — unofficial taxis are the main tourist complaint.
Russian is understood almost everywhere and Kazakh is the state language; English remains limited outside big-city hotels. A translation app goes a long way.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: Around 80 nationalities — including all EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Japan and China — enter visa-free for up to 30 days per visit. CIS and EAEU citizens enter freely for longer stays. Most other travelers can apply for a tourist eVisa on the official Visa-Migration Portal; the rest go through an embassy.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kazakhstan visa-free?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors get up to 30 days per entry, capped at 90 days in total within any 180-day period. Leaving and re-entering resets the 30-day clock but not the 90-day cap. For longer stays you need a visa or residence permit.

faq.question: Do I need to register after arriving in Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: You don't register yourself — your host does. Hotels notify the migration service automatically; private hosts must file an arrival notification within 3 working days of your arrival. Keep evidence of where you stayed in case officers ask on departure.

faq.question: How does the Kazakhstan eVisa work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities apply online at the Visa-Migration Portal (vmp.gov.kz) for a single-entry tourist eVisa, typically issued within about a week for a fee in the region of US$80. It allows a stay of up to 30 days and is used at any international airport and most land crossings. Confirm your intended crossing accepts eVisas.

faq.question: Can Russian and other CIS citizens enter Kazakhstan without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Citizens of Russia and most CIS/EAEU states enter visa-free — many on internal ID cards — and can stay up to 90 days within a 180-day period, subject to the usual host arrival-notification rules.
